==Problem==
How many four-digit numbers have all three of the following properties?

(I) The tens and ones digit are both 9.

(II) The number is 1 less than a perfect square.

(III) The number is the product of exactly two prime numbers.

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 0 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 1 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 2 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 3 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 4</imath>

==Solution 1==
The "Condition (II)" perfect square must end in "<imath>00</imath>" because <imath>...99+1=...00</imath> ''Condition (I)''. Four-digit perfect squares ending in "<imath>00</imath>" are <imath>{40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90}</imath>, which when squaring these numbers, gets you <imath>(1600, 2500, 3600, 4900, 6400, 8100)</imath> respectively.

''Condition (II)'' also says the number is in the form <imath>n^2-1</imath>. By the '''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Difference_of_two_squares Difference of Squares]''', <imath>n^2-1 = (n+1)(n-1)</imath>. Hence: 
*<imath>40^2-1 = (39)(41)</imath>
*<imath>50^2-1 = (49)(51)</imath>
*<imath>60^2-1 = (59)(61)</imath>
*<imath>70^2-1 = (69)(71)</imath>
*<imath>80^2-1 = (79)(81)</imath>
*<imath>90^2-1 = (89)(91)</imath>

On this list, the only number that is the product of <imath>2</imath> prime numbers (condition <imath>3</imath>) is <imath>60^2-1 = (59)(61)</imath>, so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\text{(B)\ 1}}</imath>.
